overloads.semanticRole: Returns a full, unfiltered snapshot: an object with a "processes" collection (all running processes) and, on 4D Server, a "sessions" collection (all connected user sessions).

sentinelValues.meaning: Processes and sessions - returns both "processes" and "sessions" lists (default value)
Processes only - returns only the "processes" list
Sessions only - returns only the "sessions" list

overloads.semanticRole: On 4D Server, returns a snapshot filtered (via the options constant) to just the processes list, just the sessions list, or both, across all sessions.

discriminatedBy.rule: Called with a single Integer argument (no sessionID).

params.name: sessionID
params.description: Session ID to scope the snapshot to

overloads.semanticRole: On 4D Server, returns a snapshot scoped to a single user session: by default a collection of all processes related to that session, plus a collection with a single object describing the session itself (and an additional server-only "session" property on each returned process). Returns a null object if sessionID is invalid.

discriminatedBy.rule: Called with a single Text argument (no options).

params.name: sessionID
params.description: Session ID to scope the snapshot to

sentinelValues.meaning: Processes and sessions - returns both "processes" and "sessions" lists (default value)
Processes only - returns only the "processes" list
Sessions only - returns only the "sessions" list

overloads.semanticRole: On 4D Server, returns a snapshot scoped to a single user session (sessionID) and further filtered to just the processes list, just the sessions list, or both (via options).

discriminatedBy.rule: Called with both a Text sessionID and an Integer options argument.

constraints: sessionID and options are honored only on 4D Server; when executed on 4D in remote or local mode, Process activity always returns the list of all running processes regardless of the parameters passed.
This command returns all processes, including internal processes not reachable by Process info.
Passing an invalid sessionID returns a null object.
